description.value: The study examined whether motivational dispositions measured by BIS/BAS subscales modulate neural responses during cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative emotional pictures in currently drug-free patients with major depressive disorder compared with healthy controls.

design.value: A block-design fMRI study compared 12 currently drug-free major depressed outpatients with 15 normal controls during three consecutive conditions: ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE. The order of DETACH and IMMERSE was counterbalanced across participants, and positive, negative, and neutral emotional pictures were presented within blocks.

task_description.value: The task was performed in three consecutive blocks (“ATTEND,” “DETACH,” and “IMMERSE”). During the ATTEND block, subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state elicited by the stimuli. During the DETACH block, participants interpreted the situation depicted as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events. During the IMMERSE block, subjects perceived each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.

presentation_software.value: E-Prime 2.0 (standard version), Psychology Software Tools, Sharpsburg, PA, USA

instructions.value: ATTEND: respond naturally without trying to change the emotional state. DETACH: interpret the situation as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment. IMMERSE: perceive each picture as real by imagining oneself or a loved one in the scene.

stimuli.value: Pictures selected from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS), with positive, negative, and neutral emotional content. Twenty-four trials were included in the detach/immerse condition, with 12 positive and 12 negative pictures; 36 trials were included in the attend condition, with 12 positive, 12 negative, and 12 neutral pictures.

description.value: Functional sequence was obtained with a time repetition (TR) of 2,000 ms, a flip angle of 90°, a time echo of 30 ms, an FOV of 240 × 240 mm2, a matrix of 64 × 64, a slice thickness of 4 mm, and a slice interval of 0.8 mm. Visual stimuli were presented through goggles mounted on the head coil. Three functional sessions were acquired.

description.value: Functional and structural image processing and statistical analyses were conducted with SPM8. The first trial of each block was discarded to reach magnetization equilibrium; remaining volumes were slice-time corrected, realigned to the mean volume, spatially normalized to standard MNI space, and smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: The first trial of each block (attend/detach/immerse condition) was discarded to reach the magnetization equilibrium.
Realignment to the mean volume to correct for head motion.
Spatial normalization to standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation.
Spatial smoothing by convolution with a standard 8-mm full-width at half-maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel.
ROI masks were derived from WFU PickAtlas with a threshold of p < 0.05 and an extent threshold of 5 voxels.
ROI time courses were extracted by generating the first eigenvariate of 8 mm around peak voxels using REX.

model_settings.value: BBS subscale scores were compared between groups.
Gender, group, and gender-by-group effects on motivational scores were tested.

model_type.value: whole-brain voxel-wise multiple linear regression model

model_settings.value: Each condition was modeled using a box-car function convolved with a canonical HRF. The realignment parameters were included in the models as covariates of no interest.
Between-group comparisons of whole-brain activations were conducted under each emotion regulation condition, including positive and negative detach-attend and immerse-attend contrasts.

Group, emotion and ER were entered as between-subject factors and BIS/BAS subscale scores as covariates. Interactive effects between group and motivation, and the main effect of group on emotion regulation, were examined.
A two-sample t-test was conducted with BIS/BAS scores as covariates to examine group-related differences in motivation.
For each group and each reappraisal-versus-attend contrast, BIS/BAS scores were entered as covariates of interest to identify clusters showing a linear relationship with BIS/BAS scores.

Correlations were examined between BIS/BAS scores and time courses of a priori PFC/amygdala ROIs and neural correlates of motivation-by-group interaction across ER conditions. Multiple Pearson correlations were Bonferroni corrected with a threshold of P < 0.003 (= 0.05/15).

BIS/BAS scores were entered into a generalized linear regression model to predict reappraisal-related brain activation. In an additional model for depressed patients, BDI scores were entered as a predictor together with BIS scores.
